characterization_methods.key_findings: Peak stress at 1100 °C and 0.01 s^-1 is about 65 MPa; the curve rises to a peak of about 65 MPa then softens and stays almost flat.
characterization_methods.purpose: To obtain rheological (flow) stress–strain curves and characteristic stress/strain values for the deformation condition of this sample.
characterization_methods.technique: Isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression testing (thermo-mechanical simulation)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: LEXT OLS4000 laser confocal microscope; etching solution 30% nitric acid alcohol (volume fraction)
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 1100 °C / 0.01 s^-1 the large deformation zone shows a finer, more heterogeneous grain structure with many small recrystallized grains; the degree of DRX ranks zone 3 (large) > zone 2 (small) > zone 1 (difficult).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis; three deformation zones imaged with 100 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: To observe microstructure evolution and DRX in the three deformation zones after 60% compression.
characterization_methods.technique: Optical / laser confocal metallography (after axis splitting, mounting, grinding, polishing and etching)

analytical_models.equation_role: Z = ε̇·exp(Qp/RT); characterizes the combined influence of temperature and strain rate on flow stress
analytical_models.model_note: The activation energy Qp = 669.844 kJ mol^-1 is the average value within the experimental range of the paper (derived from k1 = 5.135 and k2 = 15.690), not condition-specific. lnZ = 54.08 is the value for this sample's condition (1100 °C, 0.01 s^-1) from Table 1.

computational_details.simulation_method: Zener-Hollomon (Z) parameter calculation derived from the Arrhenius hyperbolic-sine constitutive equation

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The sample was heated to 1200 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s prior to homogenization.
Homogenized by holding at 1200 °C for 120 s.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature of 1100 °C at a rate of 5 °C/s.
Held for 15 s at the set temperature (1100 °C) before compression so the temperature difference between the inside and outside of the sample was the same.

Isothermal constant strain rate compression at 1100 °C and 0.01 s^-1 to a maximum compression of 60% (corresponding to a maximum true strain of 0.92). Mica foils with high-temperature lubricants were affixed to the two end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity. Cylindrical sample of Φ 8 mm × 12 mm.
After compression the sample was sprayed with water to cool the steel down (quenching).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression to 60% (true strain 0.92) with mica foils + high-temperature lubricant at end faces; Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator; water-spray cooled after compression.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: True stress–true strain flow curve at T = 1100 °C, 0.01 s^-1: rises to a peak of about 65 MPa, then softens and remains almost flat after the peak.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: grains are large relative to the 100 µm scale bar; individual grains span roughly one to a few times the bar length

phases_present.morphology: large polygonal grains; some grains nearly featureless light grey, others densely striped
phases_present.texture: striation direction changes grain to grain (banded segregation contrast)

structures.overall_structure: Initial (as-forged billet) microstructure of etched Fe-Mn-Al-C steel: large polygonal grains whose boundaries appear as a bright continuous etched network, enclosing dark grey grain interiors. Within essentially every grain the interior carries many fine, closely spaced parallel light-grey striations/lamellae (banded dendritic/interdendritic segregation contrast) rather than a uniform solid solution.

structures.microstructure_counts: 3 deformation zones imaged (zone 1 difficult deformation, zone 2 small deformation, zone 3 large deformation)

phases_present.morphology: coarse equiaxed grains of mixed contrast

microstructure_list.region: zone 1 (difficult deformation zone, near loading surfaces)

phases_present.morphology: similar to zone 1 but slightly finer mixed structure

microstructure_list.region: zone 2 (small deformation zone, ends near horizontal centre line)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: finer and more heterogeneous than zones 1 and 2

phases_present.morphology: finer, more heterogeneous grain structure with many small (recrystallized) grains

microstructure_list.region: zone 3 (large deformation zone, central band / core of compressed sample)

structures.overall_structure: Microstructure after 60% hot compression at 1100 °C and 0.01 s^-1 (Fig. 9(a)), observed in three deformation zones of the axially sectioned specimen. With the decrease of strain rate the recrystallized grains grew and the degree of microstructure heterogeneity improved relative to higher strain rates.

unmapped_findings: Peak (flow) stress of this sample at 1100 °C and 0.01 s^-1 is approximately 65 MPa, read from Fig. 3(b) (true stress–true strain curves at T = 1100 °C for four strain rates).

The dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the steel computed by the Arrhenius hyperbolic-sine method is 669.844 kJ mol^-1 (average value within the experimental range 900–1150 °C, 0.01–10 s^-1), based on average slopes k1 = 5.135 and k2 = 15.690.
The Zener-Hollomon parameter lnZ for this sample (1100 °C, 0.01 s^-1) is 54.08 (Table 1).

No condition-specific DRX average grain size value is reported in the text for 1100 °C / 0.01 s^-1; only a curve (Fig. 10 / Fig. 11a) is given, from which the 0.01 s^-1 series reaches just below 80 µm at 1150 °C (grain size exceeds 70 µm).

The DRX average grain size prediction model for the steel is d_rex = 807743.63·ε̇^(-0.1903)·exp(-120648.47/RT) + 4.338, with R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53% for all samples (global, not condition-specific).

The sample corresponds to Fig. 9(a) (T = 1100 °C, ε̇ = 0.01 s^-1); the paper states that at 1100 °C with decreasing strain rate the recrystallized grains grow and microstructure heterogeneity improves.
The material composition is Fe-25.14Mn-10Al-1.46C-0.053Nb (mass fraction %), rest Fe; same steel batch/composition used to confirm reproducibility under identical experimental conditions.
